title: fix(data-objectstack): a preference save waits for the in-flight load instead of reading its row again
body:
Fixes #37109
Part of objectstack-ai/cloud#4974
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户无感：控制台打开页面时，偏好写入（如记录最近访问）不再在首读未返回时多发一次单独查询，直接更新首读拿到的那条记录。
- 为云端发版前的控制台启动检查解决请求数超预算、时红时绿的问题。
- 出错时只是多一次或少一次请求，写入照常成功；可直接撤回本次改动。
- 无。

## What changes

`ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/userState.ts`

- New `LoadGate` (module-private): an adapter tracks its in-flight `load()`; `settled()` resolves once that load has settled and never rejects (the load reports its own errors).
- `createObjectStackUserStateAdapter`: each `save()` link on `saveChain` now waits for `loadGate.settled()` before `writer.upsert(items)`, so a save issued while the shared preference read is pending writes the row id the load remembers instead of sending `findExisting()` (the per-key `sys_user_preference` read with `$top=1` and the key filter).
- `createObjectStackUserPreferenceFamily` had the same shape (its load seeds each key writer via `remember`, its save chains only per key) and gets the same wait.
- Unchanged upsert paths: no remembered id falls through to find, then update or create; a create that loses the UNIQUE race re-finds and updates; saves still serialize on their chain. A failed or empty load leaves today's behaviour (find, then update or create).
- Module header's "`save()` does not use it" paragraph updated to say what a save now does.

Read first (by risk):

1. `userState.ts`, the `save()` of `createObjectStackUserStateAdapter`: the `.then(() => loadGate.settled())` link and its place on `saveChain`.
2. `userState.ts`, `createLoadGate`: `inFlight` is cleared only when the settled promise is still the current one, so an older load finishing cannot drop a newer one.
3. `userState.ts`, the family `save()`: the same link on the per-key chain.

## Tests

New top-level describe in `userState.family-12418.test.ts` (that file's held-request harness records bodies and imports both factories), driven through the real `ObjectStackAdapter` and client with held responses:

- a key adapter: two loads share one read (`key in (...)`), a `save` issued while it is pending sends nothing until the read answers, then sends exactly one `PATCH .../sys_user_preference/rec` and no per-key read;
- a family key: the same, `PATCH .../sys_user_preference/acc`;
- a failed shared read: the waiting save then sends its own per-key read and, on no row, a `POST` create.

<details><summary>Local runs (head 2 commits above merge base 1b3b1b47873)</summary>

- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/data-objectstack/src/userState`: Test Files 4 passed (4), Tests 33 passed (33).
- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/data-objectstack/`: Test Files 127 passed (127), Tests 1427 passed (1427).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack run type-check`: exit 0 (its program lists all four `userState*.test.ts` files).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack run lint`: exit 0, 0 errors (warnings pre-existing).

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (one-off, not kept)</summary>

Mutations through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each verified on disk (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed) and restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. The subject is imported from `./userState` source, so no build leg.

- Remove the wait in the key adapter's `save()`: `a key adapter writes the row the shared read returned, and sends no per-key read` goes red (`expected [...] to have a length of 1 but got 2`: the per-key read was sent); Tests 1 failed, 32 passed.
- Remove the wait in the family's `save()`: `a family key writes the row the shared read returned, and sends no per-key read` goes red the same way; Tests 1 failed, 32 passed.
- First attempt at the key leg was a no-op refused by the tool before any test ran (the replacement text was a substring of the anchor); rerun with a marker replacement as above.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The evidence is the cloud `console-boots` call list on objectstack-ai/cloud#4975 (job 138720631611): the shared read, then a per-key `ui.recent` read, then the PATCH. This PR removes the middle request when the flush beats the read; the debounce, the recents provider and the call budget are untouched, as the card scopes.
- A save now waits for a load in flight even if that load was issued after the save was queued (the wait is read when the link runs). The load never rejects, so a save cannot be stuck behind a failed read; it waits as long as the read's request takes.

## Verification

Two minutes: `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/data-objectstack/src/userState.family-12418.test.ts` from the repo root; expect the three `a save issued while the load is in flight waits for it` cases green.
